answer: To register, it submits a sonnet of its own transaction history hashed with that pulse; duplicates are rejected because no two devices share the same pulse pattern. Each agent must stake a unique opal token bound to a hardware pulse signature, refreshed every epoch. Forging a thousand sybils costs a thousand distinct staked opals plus hardware attestations, making the attack economically irrational versus honest single-agent returns. In practice, Agent0132 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
